metaTitle: Electrician SEO Services for Electrical Contractors
metaDescription: Electrician SEO services from ASP: service pages, Google Business Profile and map work, and technical fixes, measured against booked jobs. No link buying.
intro: Electrician SEO is the work of ranking your company in Google's map pack and organic results for the electrical jobs you want more of. As an electrician SEO company, ASP builds the service pages, Business Profile and technical health behind those rankings, and measures them against booked jobs.

sections.heading: What electrician SEO covers
paragraphs: SEO for an electrical contractor has two halves. The local half is your Google Business Profile, reviews and directory listings, which carry real weight for "near me" and map-pack searches. The organic half is your website: service pages, content and the technical health that lets Google read them. We run both and report them together so they don't pull against each other.

If you work at your customers' homes and businesses, Google has rules for that. Its Business Profile guidelines say a service-area business should have one profile for its central office with a designated service area, and it can't list a virtual office unless that office is staffed during business hours. We build your profile inside those rules, not around them.

sections.heading: Service pages built around how electrical work is bought
paragraphs: Your site needs a page for each kind of job you want more of. We weigh what a booked job in that service is worth to you, how much demand there is, and how strong the pages already ranking are.

Planned jobs reward pages that answer real questions. The Department of Energy says most EV drivers charge overnight at home. It also says charger installations must meet local and state codes and may need permits from the local building authority. A page that walks a homeowner through capacity, circuits and permits in your area answers what they were about to ask you on the phone.
bullets: Urgent repair pages written for the person searching from their phone
EV charger installation, including capacity and circuit work
Solar tie-in or generator work, if you offer it
Commercial electrical, with its own pages and project proof
Service area pages that describe real work in each place you cover

sections.heading: Showing your license and experience on the page
paragraphs: Most states require electricians to pass a test and hold a license, the rules vary by state, and electricians may need continuing education to keep that license. Your site is the easiest place for a buyer to see it. We put license details, named authors and real project experience on the pages where buyers look for them.

That part of the work needs you. We interview you or a senior electrician, record it, and pull out the details only your crew knows: what a job cost, what tends to fail, and what you tell a homeowner before they ask. That first-hand detail is what generic content can't copy.

sections.heading: Content that matches when people search
paragraphs: Residential electrical fires are not spread evenly across the year. A U.S. Fire Administration report on 2014 to 2016 data found that residential building electrical fires happened most often in January. The data is older, but it is a fair reason to publish winter electrical safety content before the cold arrives.

Some topics follow where the trade is heading. BLS expects electricians to keep being needed to link solar and wind power to homes and businesses. If you do solar or other generation work, give those services their own pages.

sections.heading: How much electrician SEO costs
paragraphs: Four things set the price: how big and competitive your market is, how wide your service area is, how many services and locations need pages, and how much technical debt is in the way. Market size matters because the number of contractors chasing the same searches changes from one area to the next. Across the U.S., BLS counted 61,028 private residential electrical contractor establishments in 2025; how many compete in your area is what the audit measures.

Here are ASP's published prices. Local SEO Pro, which covers the Business Profile and map-pack side, is $1,200 a month on its own. Foundation is $2,500 a month and includes Local SEO Pro, StormFront, the Content Creation Package and Housecall Pro attribution setup. Growth is $3,850 a month and adds a custom website build and paid media management. Premier is custom.
Organic SEO isn't sold here as a separate retainer with a rate card. The audit sets the scope, and you see the number before you commit. Every current option is on the pricing page.

sections.heading: How we report electrician SEO results
paragraphs: Rankings and impressions show whether your visibility is moving. Calls and form fills show whether it's reaching buyers. Booked jobs show whether the work paid. Where your CRM supports attribution, we wire the lead source through to the job, and you won't see Domain Authority as a goal in the report.

We don't buy links and we don't sell link packages. We also don't promise a timeline, because it depends on your site's history and your market. Technical fixes usually show first, on-page changes next, and new content clusters move slowest but last longest.

faqs.question: What does an electrician's website need to rank?
faqs.answer: It needs a page for each service you want more of, service area pages that describe real work in the places you cover, and clear license and contact details. Under that, the site needs clean technical health so Google can read it. Your Business Profile carries much of the weight for map-pack searches, so we report it together with the site work.

faqs.question: How long does electrician SEO take?
faqs.answer: There's no honest fixed timeline. It depends on your site's history, the technical problems in the way and how competitive your market is. Technical fixes usually show first and new content takes longest. If a quarter goes by with nothing moving, we'll tell you.

faqs.question: Do you build backlinks for electricians?
faqs.answer: No. ASP doesn't buy links or sell link packages. Links that come from useful content and real partnerships are worth having, but we don't sell them as a product.

faqs.question: Can I rank in cities where I don't have an office?
faqs.answer: Google's guidelines call for one Business Profile for your central office with a designated service area. They don't allow a virtual office unless it is staffed during business hours. For other cities, the honest route is a page on your site for each area that describes real work you do there.

faqs.question: How much does electrician SEO cost?
faqs.answer: The price depends on your market, your service area, how many services and locations you have, and your site's technical debt. Local SEO Pro, which covers the Business Profile and map pack, is $1,200 a month on its own. Organic SEO is scoped by the audit, and you see the number before you commit. Our full tiers are on the pricing page.

faqs.question: Does SEO help with Google's AI Overviews?
faqs.answer: Yes, the same work does. AI answers are built from content that is indexed, useful and trusted, so first-hand detail, clear authorship and a clean site matter there too. ASP doesn't promise AI citations, because no one controls them.
